title: SAT 04 · Properties and equivalence
description: A/B reasoning practice. Difficulty is editorial, not standardized SAT calibration.

questions.title: Stationery Sets with a Distributive Shortcut
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A stationery shop prepares \(18\) identical school sets. Each set contains \(20\) pencils and \(3\) erasers. Which calculation gives the total number of individual items in all the sets? Choose A or B and justify the choice by using the distributive property.
questions.explanation: Each set contains \(20+3=23\) items. There are \(18\) sets, so the total is \(18\times23=414\). The distributive property confirms that \(18(20+3)=18\times20+18\times3=360+54=414\). Choice A multiplies the pencils by \(18\) but adds only \(3\) erasers, instead of \(18\times3\) erasers. Thus choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Decide how many items are in one set, then multiply by the number of sets; check that every part of a set gets multiplied.

questions.title: Regrouping Chairs in an Assembly Hall
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A hall contains \(4\) sections. Each section has \(6\) rows with \(5\) chairs per row. A student proposes regrouping the multiplication to count the chairs without changing the total. Which statement is valid? Choose A or B and explain the property that makes it valid.
questions.explanation: Each section contains \(6\times5=30\) chairs, so the hall contains \(4\times30=120\) chairs. The associative property of multiplication allows \(4\times(6\times5)=(4\times6)\times5=24\times5=120\). Choice B replaces multiplication of rows and chairs with addition, which does not preserve the number of chairs. Therefore choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Count the chairs in one section first, then decide which regrouping of the three factors keeps the same product.

questions.title: Identical Supply Packs across Three Days
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A school receives packs of art paper on three days, as shown in the chart. Each pack contains \(6\) sheets. A volunteer wants to use one multiplication after adding the pack counts. Which expression correctly gives the total number of sheets? Choose A or B and show why the expression is equivalent to counting each day separately.
questions.explanation: The chart shows \(12+8+10=30\) packs in total. Since every pack contains \(6\) sheets, the school receives \(30\times6=180\) sheets. By the distributive property, \((12+8+10)6=12(6)+8(6)+10(6)=72+48+60=180\). In choice A, multiplication is applied only to the \(10\) Wednesday packs, not to all three days, so it gives \(12+8+60=80\). Hence choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Bar chart of art-paper deliveries: 12 packs on Monday, 8 packs on Tuesday, and 10 packs on Wednesday. Each pack contains six sheets.

questions.hint: Add the packs for all three days first; the multiplication by 6 must apply to that whole sum.

questions.title: Two Joined Rectangular Garden Beds
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A rectangular garden is \(4\) meters tall and is divided vertically into two smaller rectangles with widths \(5\) meters and \(7\) meters. The diagram shows the shared border. Which expression correctly finds the combined area of the two beds without counting any region twice? Choose A or B and justify the equivalence using the distributive property.
questions.explanation: The two rectangles have the same height, \(4\) meters, and their widths add to \(5+7=12\) meters. The combined area is \(4\times12=48\) square meters. Applying the distributive property gives \(4(5+7)=4(5)+4(7)=20+28=48\). Choice B multiplies the two widths instead of adding them. That is not the area of either the entire garden or the sum of its two pieces. Therefore choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: A 12-meter-wide, 4-meter-tall rectangle has a vertical divider 5 meters from its left edge, making two rectangles of widths 5 and 7 meters. Corners A(0,0), B(12,0), C(12,4), D(0,4), with divider E(5,0) to F(5,4).

questions.hint: Both beds share the same height: either combine their widths or add their two areas, and check that the routes agree.

questions.title: Counting Wristbands without Double-Counting
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: There are \(32\) students. Of these, \(18\) join the chess club, \(16\) join the robotics club, and \(7\) join both clubs, as shown in the Venn diagram. Each student who joins at least one club receives exactly \(4\) wristbands, regardless of whether the student joins both. Which calculation gives the number of wristbands distributed? Choose A or B and justify the calculation using the distributive property and the overlapping group.
questions.explanation: The \(7\) students in both clubs must be counted only once. The total number of distinct members is \(18+16-7=27\). Four wristbands per member gives \(4\times27=108\). Equivalently, the disjoint Venn regions give \(4(11+7+9)=44+28+36=108\), an application of the distributive property. Choice A counts the overlapping \(7\) students twice, distributing \(28\) extra wristbands. Choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Venn diagram of 32 students: 11 only in chess, 9 only in robotics, 7 in both clubs, and 5 in neither. Thus chess has 18 members and robotics has 16.

questions.hint: Count each student who joined at least one club exactly once, using the overlap in the diagram, then multiply by the wristbands per student.

questions.title: Negative Distribution from a Function Mapping
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A machine follows the rule \(f(x)=-3(2x-5)\). The mapping diagram shows outputs for three inputs. Which expanded formula is equivalent to the original rule for every real \(x\)? Choose A or B and prove the result by distributing the negative factor.
questions.explanation: Distribute \(-3\) to both terms: \(-3(2x-5)=(-3)(2x)+(-3)(-5)=-6x+15\). The second product is positive because multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive result. The mapping verifies this formula: \(f(-1)=21\), \(f(0)=15\), and \(f(2)=3\). Choice A incorrectly keeps the constant term negative; for example, it produces \(-15\) instead of \(15\) when \(x=0\). Choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: A mapping diagram for f(x)=-3(2x-5): input -1 maps to 21, 0 maps to 15, and 2 maps to 3.

questions.hint: Multiply -3 by each term inside the parentheses, watching the sign of -3 times -5; check your result with x=0 from the mapping.

questions.title: Finding an Equivalent Formula from a Table
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table shows exact values of a linear relationship for \(x=1,2,3\). The relationship is also known to have the formula \(y=6x+10\) for all real \(x\). Which factored expression is equivalent to this formula for every real \(x\)? Choose A or B and justify your answer using distribution and one or more table entries.
questions.explanation: The distributive property gives \(2(3x+5)=2(3x)+2(5)=6x+10\), which is exactly the given rule. The table confirms it: at \(x=1\), \(y=16\); at \(x=2\), \(y=22\); and at \(x=3\), \(y=28\). Choice B expands to \(6x+20\), giving \(26\), \(32\), and \(38\) instead, so it is not equivalent. Therefore choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: A table with x values 1, 2, and 3 paired with y values 16, 22, and 28, respectively.

questions.hint: Expand each option by distributing the 2, then compare with 6x+10 or test one row of the table.

questions.title: Distributing a Fraction across a Difference
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A student rewrites \(\frac34(8x-12)\), where \(x\) is any real number. Which result is equivalent to the original expression for every real \(x\)? Choose A or B and explain how the fraction affects both terms.
questions.explanation: Multiply both terms inside the parentheses by \(\frac34\): \(\frac34(8x-12)=\frac34(8x)-\frac34(12)=6x-9\). The factor \(\frac34\) applies to \(12\) as well as to \(8x\). Choice B multiplies the first term correctly but leaves the second term unchanged. For instance, when \(x=0\), the original expression equals \(-9\), while choice B equals \(-12\). Therefore choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Multiply the 3/4 by both terms inside the parentheses, not only by the first one.

questions.title: Expanding a Quadratic Shown on a Graph
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The graph represents \(f(x)=(x-3)^2-4\), an upward-opening parabola. Which polynomial is exactly the same function for all real \(x\)? Choose A or B and explain how expanding the square agrees with the graph.
questions.explanation: Using the identity \((a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2\), we get \((x-3)^2=x^2-6x+9\). Subtracting \(4\) gives \(x^2-6x+5\), so choice B is the equivalent polynomial. The graph has vertex \((3,-4)\) and x-intercepts at \(1\) and \(5\), consistent with \(x^2-6x+5=(x-1)(x-5)\). Choice A omits the factor of \(2\) in the middle term: at \(x=3\) it gives \(-13\), not the graphed value \(-4\). Therefore choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Upward-opening parabola f(x)=(x-3)^2-4 with vertex (3,-4), x-intercepts at (1,0) and (5,0), and y-intercept at (0,5).

questions.hint: Expand (x-3)^2 as the square of a difference, then subtract 4; check one graphed point, such as the vertex.

questions.title: Cancellation without Extending the Domain
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Consider the rational expression \(R(x)=\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}\). Someone factors and cancels to get \(x+3\). Which statement describes the exact set of real numbers on which this simplification preserves the value of the original expression? Choose A or B and explain the domain restriction.

options.label: B
options.text: \(R(x)=x+3\) for every real \(x\ne3\), but \(R(3)\) is undefined.

questions.explanation: Factor the numerator as \(x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)\). For \(x\ne3\), cancellation gives \(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}=x+3\). However, at \(x=3\) the original denominator equals zero, so the original expression has no value. Cancellation never makes this excluded input valid. Choice A treats the simplified formula as if it extended the original domain, which is incorrect. Choice B gives both the equivalent expression and its correct restriction.
questions.hint: Factor the numerator and cancel, but ask whether the original expression has any value at the input that makes its denominator zero.

questions.title: Simplifying Powers and Quotients
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For nonzero real numbers \(x\) and \(y\), simplify \(\frac{(2x^2y)^3}{4xy^2}\). Which expression is equivalent on this stated domain? Choose A or B and justify each exponent operation.
questions.explanation: First apply the power of a product: \((2x^2y)^3=2^3x^{2\cdot3}y^3=8x^6y^3\). Divide by \(4xy^2\) to obtain \(\frac{8}{4}x^{6-1}y^{3-2}=2x^5y\). The restrictions \(x\ne0\) and \(y\ne0\) ensure that the original denominator is nonzero. Choice B incorrectly fails to subtract the denominator's exponent of \(x\). Thus choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Raise every factor inside the parentheses to the third power, then divide like bases by subtracting exponents.

questions.title: An Absolute-Value Identity on the Real Line
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For every real number \(x\), consider the expression \(|x-4|+|x+4|\). Which proposed simplification is valid for all real \(x\)? Choose A or B and justify your answer by analyzing the regions \(x<-4\), \(-4\le x\le4\), and \(x>4\).
questions.explanation: When \(x>4\), both quantities inside the absolute values are positive, so the sum is \((x-4)+(x+4)=2x=2|x|\). When \(x<-4\), both are negative, so the sum is \((4-x)+(-x-4)=-2x=2|x|\). Between \(-4\) and \(4\), the sum is \((4-x)+(x+4)=8=2(4)\), including the endpoints. Combining the three cases gives \(2\max(|x|,4)\) for all real \(x\). Choice B fails inside the middle interval; at \(x=0\), the original sum equals \(8\), not \(0\). Therefore choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Remove the absolute value bars separately in each region, using the sign of x-4 and of x+4 there.

questions.title: One Sticker Left in Every Box
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A fair has \(37\) boxes in one storage room and \(63\) boxes in another. Every box originally contains exactly \(19\) stickers. The organizers remove exactly \(18\) stickers from every box to give away. How many stickers remain in the two rooms combined? Choose A or B and show both a distributive shortcut and a check using the separate rooms.
questions.explanation: There are \(37+63=100\) boxes. Each box retains \(19-18=1\) sticker, so the combined remainder is \((37+63)(19-18)=100(1)=100\) stickers. Checking by room gives \(37(19-18)=37\) and \(63(19-18)=63\); adding them yields \(37+63=100\). The distributive property ensures both methods agree. Choice B, \(100\times19=1900\), counts stickers before any are removed and ignores the \(18\) stickers given away from every box. Therefore choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Find how many stickers remain in one box, then use the total number of boxes in both rooms.

questions.title: Fixing an Incorrect Distributive Calculation
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A student wants to evaluate \(24\times(30+7)\) by using the distributive property. The student writes \(24\times30+7=727\), forgetting to multiply the \(7\) by \(24\). How many must be added to the student's incorrect total to obtain the correct result? Choose A or B and explain the missing multiplication without using algebra.
questions.explanation: The correct distributive calculation is \(24\times30+24\times7=720+168=888\). The student calculated \(720+7=727\), so the missing amount is \(888-727=161\). Another way is to compare the intended \(24\times7=168\) with the \(7\) already included: \(168-7=161\). Choice A would add the full \(168\) even though the student has already counted \(7\), making the corrected result too large. Therefore choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Work out what 24 times 7 should contribute, and compare it with the 7 the student actually added.

questions.title: Simplifying a Difference of Two Squares
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For every real \(x\), a student wants to simplify \(E(x)=\frac{3(x+2)-2(x-1)}{2}+\frac{(x+1)^2-(x-1)^2}{4}\). Which single fraction is equivalent to \(E(x)\) for every real \(x\)? Choose A or B and justify the equivalence by carefully distributing and factoring the square difference.
questions.explanation: In the first numerator, distribute the negative coefficient: \(3(x+2)-2(x-1)=3x+6-2x+2=x+8\). For the second numerator, use the difference of squares: \((x+1)^2-(x-1)^2=[(x+1)-(x-1)][(x+1)+(x-1)]=2(2x)=4x\). Thus \(E(x)=\frac{x+8}{2}+\frac{4x}{4}=\frac{x+8}{2}+x=\frac{3x+8}{2}\). Choice A omits the additional \(4\) produced when \(-2\) multiplies \(-1\) and the terms are combined. At \(x=0\), the original expression is \(4\), while choice A is \(2\). Therefore choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Simplify each numerator first: distribute carefully in the first and use a difference of squares in the second; then combine over a common denominator.

questions.title: Perimeter of Joined Rooms without the Interior Wall
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Two rectangular rooms are joined along a wall of length \(4\) meters. The first room has width \(x\) meters, the second has width \(x+5\) meters, and both have height \(4\) meters in the floor plan, where \(x>0\). The divider is an interior wall and is not part of the outside perimeter. Which expression gives the outside perimeter for every allowed \(x\)? Choose A or B and justify your answer using equivalent calculations.
questions.explanation: The combined shape is a single rectangle of total width \(x+(x+5)=2x+5\) meters and height \(4\) meters. Its outside perimeter is \(2[(2x+5)+4]=2(2x+9)=4x+18\) meters. Alternatively, the two separate room perimeters add to \(2(x+4)+2(x+5+4)=4x+26\), but this counts the shared \(4\)-meter divider twice; subtracting \(2(4)=8\) gives \(4x+18\). Choice B is the sum of the separate perimeters without removing the interior wall. Therefore choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Treat the joined rooms as one large rectangle, or add the two room perimeters and decide what to do about the interior wall.

questions.title: An Extraneous Root after Rational Simplification
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Solve the equation \(\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}=\frac{8x}{x+1}\) over the real numbers. Which option gives exactly the valid solution set of the original equation? Choose A or B, first state the excluded inputs, and then explain any root rejected after simplifying.
questions.explanation: The denominators require \(x\ne3\) and \(x\ne-1\). For permitted \(x\), factor the numerator and cancel: \(\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}=\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}=x+3\). Then \(x+3=\frac{8x}{x+1}\). Multiplying by \(x+1\) gives \((x+3)(x+1)=8x\), so \(x^2+4x+3=8x\) and \(x^2-4x+3=(x-1)(x-3)=0\). The candidates are \(x=1\) and \(x=3\), but \(x=3\) makes the original left denominator zero and must be excluded. Checking \(x=1\) gives \(\frac{1-9}{1-3}=4\) and \(\frac{8}{2}=4\). Choice A mistakenly retains the forbidden root \(3\); choice B is correct.
questions.hint: List the inputs that make any denominator zero, then simplify and solve; check each candidate against that list.

questions.title: An Absolute-Value Quotient with an Exceptional Equality
questions.learningObjective: Apply properties and equivalence and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Let \(F(x)=\frac{(x-2)(x+3)}{|x-2|}\) with real \(x\ne2\). For which real inputs in its domain is \(F(x)\) exactly equal to \(x+3\)? Choose A or B and justify the complete solution set by considering the sign of \(x-2\), including possible special values where both sides are zero.
questions.explanation: For \(x>2\), the absolute value is \(|x-2|=x-2\), so \(F(x)=x+3\); every such input works. For \(x<2\), \(|x-2|=-(x-2)\), so \(F(x)=-(x+3)\). Equality with \(x+3\) then requires \(-(x+3)=x+3\), giving \(2(x+3)=0\) and \(x=-3\), which lies in the case \(x<2\). At \(x=-3\), both expressions equal zero, so this exception is valid. The input \(x=2\) remains excluded because the original denominator is zero. Thus the solution set is \(x>2\) together with \(x=-3\). Choice B overlooks the zero-factor exception and is incomplete; choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Split into the cases x>2 and x<2 to remove the absolute value, and in the second case look for an input where both sides could be zero.
